blocks.prompt: Which tool are you using today?

blocks.content:
### While the video plays

Six things to catch. Short answers. The last two are the ones the whole video is built toward, so do not pack up early.

blocks.prompt: ATMs automated counting cash. What happened to the number of tellers, and why?
Name one job in the video that disappeared and one that did not, both heavily automated.
Which number in the video surprised you most? Write the number and why.
In one sentence: what does the video say actually gets automated?
The closing statement. What is the final claim the video lands on, in your own words?
The footnotes at the end. What do they add, qualify, or complicate about the claim you just wrote down?

modules.intro: Pick one question and write your answer before we start. You will be asked for it. None of these has a correct answer.
modules.title: Discussion

blocks.content:
**D1.** Name a job where the task gets automated and the job does **not** grow. Why is yours different?

**D2.** Elevator operator is gone. Airline pilot is not. Both jobs were heavily automated. What is the actual difference?

**D3.** If most of today's jobs did not exist in 1940, can anyone predict which jobs go next? Including the video?

**D4.** What part of an engineer's job is hardest to automate? What part is easiest? Defend both.

**D5.** Argue against the video. What is the strongest case that this time really is different?

blocks.prompt: Which question did you pick, and what is your answer?

modules.intro: You run every prompt yourself. Everyone is on a different tool, so your answers will not match your neighbor's. That is the point. Fill each row as the block runs, not after.
modules.title: Four Levels, Live

columns.tip: The real page you opened, not the model.
columns.label: Checked against

blocks.content:
### Block 1 · OFF · no AI

No AI. Go to matweb.com, find the density of **6061-T6 aluminum** yourself, and record the number and the page.

This is the number every other block gets measured against.

### Block 2 · COACH · reasoning only, nothing to verify

> Explain why two aluminum alloys can have nearly the same density but very different strength. Do not give me any specific numbers.

Did a number show up anyway? Put it in Notes.

### Block 3 · ASSIST · check against Block 1

> What is the density of 6061-T6 aluminum in g/cm3?

### Block 4 · ASSIST · check this one hard

> Give me the OnlineMetals part number and current price for a 1 inch diameter 6061-T6 aluminum round bar, 12 inches long.

Open onlinemetals.com and search that exact product. Does the part number exist? Does the price match?

### Block 5 · OPEN · AI drives

> I have four unlabeled metal and plastic samples, a digital caliper, a precision scale, and a graduated cylinder. Propose a procedure to identify each one.

blocks.prompt: Blocks 3 and 4 ran at the same level on the same tool. One held up, one did not. What is different about the two questions?
Block 5. Answer this yourself, without asking the tool: why use displacement instead of just measuring the dimensions?
